messages:
jess-release: scheduling a late-night release for the SDK (py + ts) at 02:30 UTC. Plan: canary -> hold/manual -> ramp -> GA. We're retiring the old sync client (v1) and shipping async v2 as the default. I'll need a manual thumbs-up between canary and ramp.

nate-eng: noted. I'll cut artifacts and tag them as `canary` for the initial cohort. Will also create a `legacy` dist-tag for npm so current installs keep resolution. For PyPI we'll keep 1.x branch and ship a 1.9.x maintenance patch if needed.

leo-pkg: package ops checklist:
- npm: `npm publish --tag canary` then `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.0-canary canary`
- py: build wheels/sdists, `twine upload dist/*` to testpypi then pypi.
- sign artifacts and attach SHASUMs to the release page.

olivia-docs: docs blurb ready. I'll post the deprecation banner and a short migration snippet to the migration guide. Also adding a small FAQ about pinned installs and how to opt into legacy.

kai-sre: monitoring/rollback criteria I propose: immediate rollback if any of the following during a 5m sliding window:
- 5xx rate >= 1% (sustained for 2 consecutive 5m windows)
- schema validation errors exceed 0.3%
- client-side parse failures > 0.5%
Alerts route -> #incidents and page oncall. Also will run a synthetic hitting canary endpoints every 15s.

jess-release: rollback runbook (short):
1) stop the stagger in deploy-bot and revoke the canary tag: `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary`
2) for npm: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@<previous> latest` and publish patched 1.x if necessary
3) for PyPI: do not yank; publish 1.9.x.post1 patched release and point docs at pinned install instructions
4) open triage thread, attach failing request samples + failing smoke logs, and tag for postmortem.

taylor-qe: smoke tests to run during canary (run in order):
```
# TS quick smoke
NODE_ENV=production node tests/smoke/chat_quick.js --target canary
# PY quick smoke
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install redwood-sdk==2.0.0rc0 --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple
python tests/smoke/test_end2end.py::test_basic_chat
```
I'll kick off repeated runs for the first 30m.

deploy-bot: [automated] Release schedule created by jess-release for 2025-01-12T02:30:00Z. Jobs: build:py, build:ts, publish:canary, docs-deploy. Default flags can be overridden by release owner.

nate-eng: I'll set deploy flags: `--cohort 3% --stagger 10m --auto-promote false --timeout 25m --monitor-channel #devex`

leo-pkg: also adding an audit tag: `git tag -a release/sdk-2.0.0-canary -m "canary release 2.0.0"` and pushing to origin for traceability.

jess-release: starting preflight in ~15m to build artifacts and run unit tests. ping this thread when deploy-bot posts "publish started". :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [automated] Preflight builds passed. Artifacts created: `@redwood/sdk@2.0.0-canary.tgz`, `redwood_sdk-2.0.0rc1-py3-none-any.whl`. Waiting for manual trigger to publish canary.

kai-sre: dashboard ready with canary filter and synthetic probes. We'll track median latency, p50/p95, 5xx rate, and exact-match schema failures. Set alert thresholds per the earlier message.

jess-release: triggering canary now. Remember manual hold after first window.

deploy-bot: [automated] Canary published to 3% cohort. Health pings will be posted every 2m to this thread and to #devex.

taylor-qe: first 10m smoke: TS smoke passed, PY smoke failed once with a missing field in response. Capturing logs and re-running.

kai-sre: monitoring initial window: 5xx at 0.05% stable, schema validation errors 0.04% -> green. We saw taylor-qe's missing field but it's an isolated parse; collecting request sample.

nate-eng: investigating the missing field. quick grep in recent commits shows a small renaming of `user_id` -> `uid` in a helper serialization layer. pushing hotfix to canary branch now.

leo-pkg: if hotfix lands, we can re-release canary artifact but keep cohort paused until confirmation. Avoid publishing to latest tag.

jess-release: can we set `--auto-promote false` for the job? Confirmed earlier but making explicit: manual promote required.

deploy-bot: [automated] Manual promotion is disabled for this release. Cohort remains at 3% until user confirm.

nate-eng: hotfix pushed and new canary artifact built. Will not bump dist-tags. Asking QE to re-run smoke.

taylor-qe: re-ran PY smoke, now passes. TS still green. Recommending promote to 15% after a second 30m hold.

kai-sre: second window (3% with hotfix) metrics normal. No sustained spikes.

jess-release: OK promote to 15% when ready. Also reminder: add a short note in release notes about the rename and migration snippet for `user_id -> uid`.

leo-pkg: ops publish commands for runbook:
```
# publish canary
npm publish --tag canary
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.0-canary canary
# roll latest back if needed
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.9.9 latest
# py
python -m build && twine upload --repository pypi dist/*
```

jess-release: decision: move to 15% now, hold manual again before GA. If 15% stable overnight we'll schedule GA tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Any objections?

nate-eng: no objections. :+1:

olivia-docs: I'll schedule the docs banner flip to go live at GA time; for now, staging banner and migration guide linked in release notes.

kai-sre: adding one emergency clause: if malformed responses exceed 0.2% for two consecutive 5m windows during the 15% window, rollback immediately.

jess-release: agreed. final note: avoid PyPI yanks; prefer patch and republish. For npm tag removal is fine but we won't unpublish. Ok good work team, watch channel and I'll post next update after the 15% window. :rocket
